CVE-2026-102963.title: Use-after-return in getaddrinfo() when a DNS query that followed a CNAME cannot be cancelled
CVE-2026-102963.description:
dns_resolve_cancel_with_name() in subsys/net/lib/dns/resolve.c looks up the pending query to cancel by DNS id plus a hash of the name the caller originally asked for. When a reply contains only a CNAME, the resolver sends a new query for the alias and overwrites the slot's query_hash with the hash of the alias name. After one or more CNAME hops, cancelling by the original name silently fails with -ENOENT and the query stays pending.

zsock_getaddrinfo() (exec_query() in subsys/net/lib/sockets/getaddrinfo.c) passes a pointer to its stack-local ai_state as the resolver callback context. When its semaphore wait times out, it calls dns_cancel_addr_info_with_name(), ignores the result, and returns. The CNAME re-query restarts the resolver timer, so a CNAME-only response that arrives more than about 100 ms after the query lets the getaddrinfo() wait expire first. CVE-2026-126367.title: @grpc/grpc-js: safe_regex incorrectly applies partial string matching for patterns with alternation
CVE-2026-126367.description: @grpc/grpc-js implements the core functionality of gRPC purely in JavaScript, without a C++ addon. Before 1.13.2, and from 1.14.0 through 1.14.1, the @grpc/grpc-js-xds SafeRegexValueMatcher and PathSafeRegexValueMatcher add start and end anchors without grouping a supplied top-level alternation. An expression intended to match one of several complete values can therefore match a prefix, substring, or suffix. The affected matchers are used for route selection, xDS credential identity matching, and RBAC URL path, principal name, server name, and header rules. An ALLOW policy using an alternation can consequently accept a method, certificate identity, or header value outside the intended set, while a DENY policy becomes broader rather than permissive. This issue is fixed in versions 1.13.2 and 1.14.2.

CVE-2026-99441.title: nvmet-auth: serialize access to DH-HMAC-CHAP state to fix UAF
CVE-2026-99441.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nvmet-auth: serialize access to DH-HMAC-CHAP state to fix UAF

A REPLY AUTH_SEND command can derive a dhchap_skey key while a
concurrent AUTH_RECEIVE command observing this REPLY state executes
the failure path and frees that key. The REPLY command then continues
and writes into freed memory, causing a use-after-free. KASAN reports
it as:

BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in __sha256_final
Write of size 4 at addr ffff88800359c540
...
nvmet_auth_sq_free (drivers/nvme/target/auth.c:237)
nvmet_execute_auth_receive (drivers/nvme/target/fabrics-cmd-auth.c:621)

Add a mutex to each submission queue to serialize authentication
commands and timeout handling. Unlock the mutex before completing
requests and ignore outdated timeout callbacks. Limit timeout delays
to prevent immediate expiry on 32-bit kernels.
